purpose: Adds an opt-in complexity heuristic for dynamic per-file token budget allocation in code reviews, saving tokens on simple files while giving complex files full context. The feature is backward-compatible and disabled by default.
riskRationale: Core implementation is well-designed and backward-compatible, but a critical config-propagation gap in both the Action and App entry points silently drops YAML tokenBudget settings, making the feature unusable via its documented opt-in mechanism.

text: This PR introduces a well-structured, opt-in complexity heuristic with clean typing, proper backward compatibility, and solid test coverage. However, a critical config-propagation bug in both the Action and App entry points prevents users from enabling the feature via YAML as documented, making it effectively dead on arrival. A significant DRY violation where budget allocation logic is duplicated across two methods also creates maintenance risk. These issues should be addressed before merge.

reasoning: The config-propagation bug in both the Action and App entry points silently drops YAML review.tokenBudget settings, preventing users from enabling the feature as documented. This must be fixed before merge.

message: Default config sets enabled:false, ensuring zero impact on existing deployments with clean backward compatibility.
Complexity heuristic uses lightweight regex and brace counting on diff patch text alone — no file I/O or AST parsing — keeping the approach scalable.
Four comprehensive test cases cover simple file reduction, complex file full context, disabled mode backward compat, and no-patch edge case.
Cross-field constraint enforcement ensuring simpleThreshold ≤ complexityThreshold at validation time is a thoughtful guard against misconfiguration.

YAML config review.tokenBudget is silently dropped when building AgentConfig. The review object spreads DEFAULT_CONFIG.review (with enabled:false) and only overrides inline, never propagating loadedConfig?.review?.tokenBudget. Users who set review.tokenBudget.enabled:true in .opencode-reviewer.yml get the default disabled behavior with no warning.
suggestion: Spread loadedConfig?.review?.tokenBudget into the review object to propagate YAML token budget settings to the runtime config.

message: Same config-propagation gap as the Action entry point. buildConfig() only spreads DEFAULT_CONFIG.review and overrides inline. No mechanism exists to set tokenBudget via environment variable or any other means.
suggestion: Add a tokenBudget override mechanism, either by reading a structured environment variable or by making the config function accept and merge a partial PromptConfig.

message: Budget allocation logic is duplicated between computeTokenBudgetMetrics and buildPRContextString. Both methods independently implement the same complexity classification (complex/simple/interpolation), linear interpolation, and effective-cap clamping. Any future change to one without the other will silently produce inconsistent metrics vs. the actual context sent to the model.
suggestion: Extract a shared private helper (e.g. computeEffectiveCap(score, tokenBudgetConfig, maxLines): { effectiveCap, category }) used by both buildPRContextString and computeTokenBudgetMetrics.

message: Double logging in multi-batch path: logTokenSavings is called unconditionally at line 405 (before synthesis check) AND again in every exit path (line 450 on success, line 473 on parse failure). This means metrics are logged twice on the common success path.
suggestion: Remove the early logTokenSavings call at lines 405-409 and add logging in the synthesis-failure path (around line 411) so it fires exactly once per exit path, matching the behavior of the success and parse-failure paths.

message: The controlFlowRegex operates on the raw patch text, which includes diff metadata like hunk headers (@@ -... +... @@) and file path lines (--- a/..., +++ b/...). Keywords like 'case', 'if', 'for' could appear in these metadata lines (e.g. a file path like src/case-study.ts), inflating the complexity score.
suggestion: Filter the regex match to only scan patch lines that start with '+' or '-' (actual diff content), or strip hunk header lines before matching.

message: TokenBudgetConfigSchema lacks a .refine() to enforce the cross-field constraint simpleThreshold ≤ complexityThreshold. The constraint is only enforced by validateConfig() in config.ts, so configs validated through AgentConfigSchema.parse() (bypassing validateConfig) can produce invalid threshold relationships.
suggestion: Add a .refine() to TokenBudgetConfigSchema for the cross-field constraint.

message: The logTokenSavings message reports 'N simple, M complex' but files whose complexity falls in the interpolation range (between simpleThreshold and complexityThreshold) are not counted in either group, making the breakdown incomplete.
suggestion: Add a third counter for files in the interpolation range and include it in the log message (e.g. 'N simple, M medium, P complex'), or clarify that the counts only cover files at the extremes.

message: Test 'complex file gets full context when token budget is enabled' only asserts that the context contains 'Token budget:' — it doesn't verify that the file actually received the maxLinesComplex cap or that the full patch was included. A regression that accidentally lowers the budget for complex files would still pass.
suggestion: Add assertions verifying that the complexity score exceeds the threshold and that the context includes the full patch (or the expected truncated length).

message: In the multi-batch path, buildPRContextString computes budgetMetrics for each batch, but the returned object is immediately destructured to discard metrics. Meanwhile computeTokenBudgetMetrics recomputes the same metrics from scratch on the full files array, resulting in N+1 redundant metric computations per multi-batch review.
suggestion: If the DRY refactor is implemented with a shared helper, both calls share the same computation. Alternatively, have buildPRContextString skip metric tracking when called from the batch path via an optional parameter.
